candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize informed consent as an informed, voluntary decision by a patient with decision-making capacity rather than merely obtaining a signature.

options.A: A signature alone is sufficient even if the procedure has not been explained
options.B: The patient receives adequate information about the procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives and voluntarily decides while able to make the decision
options.C: Consent is most valid when obtained after sedation so the patient is less anxious
options.D: A family member should sign whenever one is available, even if the patient has decision-making capacity

candidate.rationale: CMS requires hospital informed-consent processes to contain information that allows patients or their representatives to make fully informed decisions about care. HHS policy analysis describes informed consent in terms of adequate disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternatives and the core elements of being informed, voluntary, and competent. A signature alone does not create valid informed consent, and a capable patient ordinarily makes the decision personally.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hospital consent processes must support fully informed decisions; informed consent includes adequate disclosure of risks, benefits, and alternatives and an informed, voluntary decision by a competent decision-maker.

candidate.source_organization: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) / U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)
